extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates, graduate students, and researchers in mathematical logic / model theory
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of second-order logic semantics, expressiveness, and proof-theoretic reductions (Skolemization, Herbrand expansions), plus many-sorted and general-structure treatments. Contains theorems, examples, and constructive methods used in model theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-order satisfaction with assignment function
rubrics_metrics.description: Let V be the set of all variables (individual, predicate, or function). Let s be a function on V that assigns to each variable the suitable type of object. For a term t, s(t) is defined in the natural way (if F is a function variable then s(F t1 ... tn) is the result of applying s(F) to s(t1),...,s(tn)). Satisfaction of atomic formulas is defined analogously to first-order case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline semantic clause: s assigns individuals to individual variables, n-ary relations to predicate variables, and n-ary operations to function variables; evaluation of compound terms and atomic formulas follows by applying these assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic satisfaction for predicate variables
rubrics_metrics.description: |=A X t1 ... tn [s] iff s(t1), ..., s(tn) ∈ s(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct definition: an atomic formula formed with a predicate variable X holds under assignment s exactly when the tuple of the interpreted argument terms lies in the relation assigned to X by s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantics of second-order universal predicate quantifier
rubrics_metrics.description: |=A ∀ Xn_i ϕ[s] iff for every n-ary relation R on |A|, ϕ[s(Xn_i | R)] holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universal quantification over predicate variables ranges over all n-ary relations on the domain |A| (full semantics). Analogous clause for universal function quantifiers ranges over all functions |A|^n → |A|.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation comprehension validity
rubrics_metrics.description: For any formula ϕ in which the predicate variable Xn does not occur free, the formula ∃ Xn ∀ v1 ... ∀ vn [Xn v1 ... vn ↔ ϕ] is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Says there exists a relation consisting exactly of the n-tuples satisfying ϕ (full comprehension/schema for relations). Other variables may be free in ϕ; this is called a relation comprehension formula (similarly for function comprehension under unique-existence conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Function comprehension validity (unique-existence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ψ is a formula in which the function variable Fn does not occur free and ∀ v1...vn ∃! vn+1 ψ holds then ∃ Fn ∀ v1...vn+1 (Fn v1...vn = vn+1 ↔ ψ) is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a unique-existence proviso for the output; this yields existence of a function whose graph is exactly the tuples satisfying ψ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-order expression of well-ordering and completeness properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples showing standard mathematical properties can be expressed as single second-order sentences: e.g., well-ordering, the least-upper-bound property for R, Peano induction ∀ X(X0 ∧ ∀ y(Xy → XSy) → ∀ y Xy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text gives explicit translations (formulas) for these properties. Use of relation/function variables (and omission of irrelevant subscripts/superscripts) is allowed for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categoricity via second-order axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of second-order sentences (e.g., Peano axioms plus second-order induction) can be categorical: any model of these axioms is isomorphic to the standard structure (e.g., (N;0,S) or the real ordered field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-order quantifiers ranging over all relations/functions enable categorical characterizations that first-order schemas cannot achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-order characterization of infinitude (λ∞)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a single second-order sentence λ∞ expressing that a set is infinite, e.g., ∃ X [X transitive, irreﬂexive and domain all elements with ∀ u ∃ v Xuv], or ∃ F [F injective and not onto].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides explicit constructions showing second-order sentences can capture 'infinite' as a single sentence, contrasting with the infinite set {λ2, λ3, ...} in first-order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure of compactness in full second-order logic (Theorem 41A)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an unsatisfiable set of second-order sentences every finite subset of which is satisfiable (e.g., {¬λ∞, λ2, λ3, ...}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows compactness theorem (valid for first-order) fails under full second-order semantics. The provided example demonstrates finite satisfiability vs global unsatisfiability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure of L¨owenheim–Skolem for second-order logic (Theorem 41B)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a sentence in the second-order language of equality that is true in a set iff its cardinality is 2^{ℵ0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By expressing properties that pin down the real-ordered field (using second-order completeness/least-upper-bound), then existentially quantifying the field parameters, one can produce a sentence whose models are exactly sets of a particular cardinality; hence Lowenheim–Skolem does not hold in the same way as in first-order logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-definability and non-enumerability of second-order validities (Theorem 41C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of valid second-order sentences is not definable in N by any second-order formula; moreover it is not arithmetical and not recursively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses the second-order theory T^2 of N and Tarski-style undefinability; adding α (conjunction of AE and second-order induction) shows validity set would define T^2, contradiction; result: enumerability theorem fails for second-order logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast between second-order universal sentences and first-order schemas
rubrics_metrics.description: A second-order universal sentence (e.g., full Peano induction) asserts closure for every subset, whereas the corresponding first-order schema only asserts closure for every definable subset; models of the schema may have non-definable subsets violating intended property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why second-order induction is stronger: second-order quantification ranges over all subsets, not only definable ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skolem Normal Form Theorem (Skolemization)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any first-order formula one can find a logically equivalent prenex second-order formula of a special form: (a) a (possibly empty) string of existential individual and function quantifiers, followed by (b) a (possibly empty) string of universal individual quantifiers, followed by (c) a quantifier-free formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by examples: ∀ x ∃ y ϕ(x,y) ⇔ ∃ F ∀ x ϕ(x, F x). More complex alternations yield existential function quantifiers of higher arities. Uses axiom of choice in semantic argument constructing Skolem functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 42A: reduction of satisfiability to universal formulas with function symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: For any first-order ϕ, there exists a universal formula θ in an expanded language containing function symbols such that ϕ is satisfiable iff θ is satisfiable. Applying to ¬ϕ yields an existential formula (with function symbols) valid iff ϕ is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: replace Skolem existential function variables by new function symbols and constants (e.g., c,f,g), producing a universal θ that is 'equally satisfiable' though not logically equivalent in the original language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 42B: undecidability consequences of Skolem reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) In a recursively numbered language with a two-place predicate and infinitely many k-place function symbols, the set of Gödel numbers of satisfiable universal (first-order) sentences is not recursive. (b) The set of Gödel numbers of valid existential (first-order) sentences is not recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces arbitrary validity/satisfiability problems to these special forms; thus decision procedures for these classes would contradict Church's theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate-variable Skolem form (∃2/∀2 reductions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any first-order formula is logically equivalent to a second-order formula consisting of (a) a string of existential predicate quantifiers, followed by (b) universal individual quantifiers, followed by (c) existential individual quantifiers, followed by (d) a quantifier-free formula. This yields analogous reductions to ∀2 and ∃2 cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides approach to convert function-variable Skolemization to predicate-variable form by encoding functions as relations with uniqueness conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Herbrand's Theorem and Herbrand expansions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a set Γ of first-order sentences, replace by Skolem normal form to get a set of universal formulas (with function symbols); let H be the Herbrand universe (all ground terms) and let Γ_H be the set of all ground instances of Γ. Then either (I) Γ_H is unsatisfiable in propositional logic, whence Γ |= φ, or (II) Γ_H is satisfiable in propositional logic, yielding a truth assignment v that defines a Herbrand model H (universe H, functions interpreted autonymously, predicates defined by v) giving a counterexample to Γ |= φ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the constructive method of translating first-order satisfiability/validity questions into propositional (sentential) satisfiability via the Herbrand universe and shows how to build a first-order model from a satisfying propositional assignment. Use compactness of sentential logic to get finite unsatisfiable subset when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Herbrand expansions to prove compactness and enumerability
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ_H (the set of ground instances) is unsatisfiable then some finite subset is unsatisfiable (compactness of sentential logic), yielding compactness for first-order logic. Similarly, enumerability of validities follows by progressively generating more of Γ_H until an unsatisfiable finite set (detectable by truth-tables) appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an alternative, constructive route to compactness and enumerability using Herbrand methods rather than completeness/deductive calculus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved L¨owenheim–Skolem via Skolem functions (exercise statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a structure for a countable language and S a countable subset of |A|. There is a countable elementary substructure B of A with S ⊆ |B| such that for any assignment s mapping variables into |B| and any first-order ϕ, |=A ϕ[s] iff |=B ϕ[s].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion: choose Skolem functions for all formulas and close S under these functions. Resulting B is an elementary substructure (uses axiom of choice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Many-sorted logic syntax and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A many-sorted language has a nonempty index set I of sorts; for each sort i there are variables v^i_n, quantifier symbol ∀^i, predicate symbols for tuples of sorts, constants and function symbols typed by tuples of sorts. A many-sorted structure assigns a universe |A|_i to each sort and interprets predicates, constants, and functions accordingly. Truth/satisfaction are defined with quantifiers ranging over the corresponding sort-universes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many-sorted frameworks formalize multiple domains (e.g., individuals, relations) explicitly; universes may overlap but can be made disjoint without loss of generality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of many-sorted to one-sorted via Qi predicates and (cid:19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate each many-sorted sentence σ to a one-sorted σ* by relativizing each quantifier ∀^i v to ∀ v (Qi v → ...). Introduce one-place predicates Qi for each sort i and include sentences (cid:19): (1) ∃ v Qi v, and (2) function-compatibility axioms ∀ v1...vn (Qi1 v1 → ... → Qin vn → Qin+1 f v1 ... vn). Then Lemma 43A/B and Theorem 43C give equivalence: (Γ |= σ in many-sorted) iff (Γ* ∪ (cid:19) |= σ* in one-sorted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields reductions allowing one-sorted model-theoretic results (compactness, enumerability, Löwenheim–Skolem) to transfer to many-sorted languages; constructive details for converting structures between representations are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for many-sorted languages: compactness, enumerability, Löwenheim–Skolem
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the translation and (cid:19), one obtains: (a) Compactness theorem: if every finite subset of a many-sorted set Γ has a model then Γ has a model. (b) Enumerability theorem: for recursively numbered many-sorted languages, valid sentence Gödel numbers are recursively enumerable. (c) Löwenheim–Skolem: any many-sorted structure (countable language) has an elementarily equivalent countable structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each follows from the corresponding one-sorted theorem applied to Γ* ∪ (cid:19) and translated back to many-sorted setting via Lemmas 43A/43B and Theorem 43C.

rubrics_metrics.name: General-structure (many-sorted) approach to second-order logic and εn/En symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the second-order language as a many-sorted first-order language with ℵ0 sorts (individuals, n-place predicate sorts, n-place function sorts) and two new parameter classes: membership predicates εn (takes an n-place predicate-variable and n individual terms) and evaluation functions En (apply an n-place function-variable to n terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recasts second-order syntax into a first-order many-sorted framework, enabling alternative semantic accounts where predicate/function variables range over designated universes rather than 'all' relations/functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 44A: homomorphism to genuine-membership/evaluation structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a many-sorted structure A with disjoint universes, there is a homomorphism h of A onto a structure B such that (a) h is identity on individual universe and preserves satisfaction (|=A ϕ[s] iff |=B ϕ[h ◦ s]); (b) n-place predicate universe of B consists of certain n-ary relations on the individual universe and ε^B_n relates R and tuple iff tuple ∈ R; (c) n-place function universe of B consists of certain n-place functions on the individual universe and E^B_n(f,a1,...,an) = f(a1,...,an).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct h by mapping predicate-sort elements to the relations they 'represent' via ε^A_n and mapping function-sort elements to the functions given by E^A_n; this produces a semantically natural structure where ε and E are genuine membership/evaluation.
